Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the intro call earlier. As mentioned, we're putting together an RFP for a 12-week pilot (user-facing chat service, mixture of long-context summarization and short Q&A). Procurement asked me to share our initial workload profile and ask a few clarifying questions:  

- Expected concurrency: 120 active sessions peak (short bursts; median request latency target 150ms p95).
- Token distribution: 60% short (<=128), 30% medium (128-1024), 10% long (>1024, up to ~6k).
- Throughput goal: support sustained 6,000 token/sec average across the pool with headroom for 9,000 token/sec bursts.
- Security: SOC2 evidence will be required for the pilot; we also need to understand data retention controls in private deployments.

Attached is our RFP packet (Orion_RFP_Pilot_Specs.pdf). Can you confirm:  

1) Which GPU families would Redwood recommend for this mix (cost / latency tradeoff)?
2) Does a single reserved pool cover our burst and long-context needs or do you suggest tiering (e.g., low-latency small models + high-memory nodes for long-tail)?
3) What commitment tiers make sense for a 12-week pilot vs a production run?

Would appreciate a short written response we can pass to procurement.

Thanks,
David

Hi David — great to connect earlier. Thanks for the RFP packet. I'm looping in our solutions engineer (Monica) and Sales Ops (Lauren) to put together a concise recommendation you can hand to procurement. High-level answers below; Monica will follow with a short sizing sheet and recommended GPU blends. Lauren will flag commitment/contract flex for a 12-week pilot.

Quick answers:
1) GPU families: A mix of high-throughput A100-class (for quantized dense workloads) and one or two high-memory H100-like nodes for long-context (>4k) sessions. If cost is a primary constraint, an Ampere-generation 80GB variant with quantization can handle many medium-context flows at a lower unit cost.
2) Architecture: We usually recommend a tiered pool: a low-latency fleet (smaller models on high-io GPUs) for the 60% short requests + a high-memory lane for long-context work and batched summarization jobs. Smart routing (by latency vs cost) keeps short requests on fast paths and spills long runs to the high-memory nodes.
3) Commitment tiers: For a 12-week pilot, we can offer a time-boxed reserved pool with a flexible ramp (lower committed baseline + paid burst capacity). For production, we recommend a monthly reserved commitment calibrated to 70-80% of steady-state throughput with burst credit to handle spikes.

Monica — can you attach the intake workbook prefilled with our recommended mixes (GPU families, expected throughput per SKU, and tail-latency projections)? Lauren — could you confirm what commitment bands we can propose for a short pilot and an option for conversion to an annual reserved plan?

Best,

Karthik / Lauren — pasted my quick sizing notes below (I'll attach a CSV with scenario numbers). These are conservative but tailored to Orion's token mix + p95 latency targets.

--- Monica's sizing notes ---
Assumptions from RFP: 120 peak concurrent sessions; sustained 6k token/sec, burst 9k token/sec; token mix as David listed. Model family assumed: 13B/70B class variants (customer mentioned both during call).

Tier recommendation: 3 logical lanes
- Lane A (Low-latency conversational): 8 x A100-80GB equiv (quantized), continuous batching, expected sustained throughput ~4.5k token/sec, p95 latency ~120-180ms depending on model size. Handles ~70% of short+medium requests.
- Lane B (High-memory long-context): 2 x H100-80/90GB equiv (unquantized for long context) dedicated to >4k sequences + larger model runs, handling ~10% of workload; expected batch throughput ~800-1,200 token/sec when scheduled, tail latencies higher for very long runs.
- Lane C (Burst/Batch processing): 4 x cheaper Ampere 48GB-class nodes for batched summarization jobs and overflow; good for cost-effective throughput during scheduled batch windows. Provides burst headroom to reach ~9k token/sec aggregate when combined with Lane A.

Notes on routing and autoscale:
- Smart routing policy: prefer Lane A for conversational sessions; fallback to Lane C when Lane A is saturated; route long-context to Lane B by token-length detector.
- KV/prefix caching: recommend enabling shared KV cache for repeated context patterns to reduce effective token compute by ~8-12% in production.

Projected cost & Sizing workbook attached: includes per-GPU token/sec estimates, expected p95 latencies, and a conservative packing strategy.

I'll attach gpu-fitment-scenarios.csv with clear numbers for each lane. Happy to jump on a short call with David to walk through the tradeoffs.

Monica Patel
